svg.aria-label: How a kernel launch reaches an SM. The CPU driver writes methods into a pushbuffer in host memory and rings the GPU's doorbell register with one MMIO write, the front end reads the GPFIFO entry and fetches the methods, and the work distributor drops a thread block on an SM with room. Below, NVIDIA's V100 numbers for 2.9 µs kernels, about 9.6 µs per kernel when every kernel is synced, about 3.8 µs with one sync per step, and about 3.4 µs once the kernels sit in one CUDA graph.
